Q2 FY27 Earnings Conference Call. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only

Salila Pande: 
Thank you, Swapnali. A very good afternoon to everyone who is present on the call today. Along 
with the management team of SBI Cards, I extend a warm welcome and sincere thanks for 
joining us for the Q2 FY27 Earnings Call. 
India's growth outlook remains resilient despite an uncertain global environment. As per RBI, 
real GDP growth for FY27 is projected to be 7.1%, up from 6.7% projected earlier, reflecting 
the strength of domestic economic activity. The International Monetary Fund has also recently 
raised India's economic growth forecast to 7% for both FY27 and FY28, citing resilient domestic 
demand and strong services activity. 
 
The upward revision reinforces India's position as the world's fastest-growing major economy 
despite rising global oil prices and persistent geopolitical tensions. Against this macroeconomic 
backdrop, the growing scale of digital transactions and increasing access to formal credit are 
contributing to the development of more integrated payments and credit ecosystem.  
Digital payments ecosystem continues to scale rapidly with UPI remaining at the centre of this 
expansion. UPI transaction volumes grew 27% Y-o-Y to approximately 145 billion transactions 
during the first half of FY27, underscoring the increasing frequency and ubiquity of digital 
payments in India. 
The credit card industry continues to maintain a healthy growth trajectory with cards in force 
increasing by around 10.5% Y-o-Y to over 124 million as of August 2026. Cumulative credit 
card spends for the first 5 months of FY27 stood at more than INR10 trillion, reflecting the 
growing scale of the credit card ecosystem. 
 
The industry continues to witness evolution, both in terms of customer demographics and usage 
patterns. As per the industry reports, credit card customer base is becoming younger and more 
diverse. Nearly half of the first-time credit card users are now aged 30 or below, while 
approximately 46% of the new users are coming from semi-urban, Tier 2, Tier 3 and rural 
markets. 
This reflects the growing democratization of credit and the expanding opportunity to serve 
customers beyond traditional metropolitan centres. As a customer-centric organization, SBI 
Card understands this and is well positioned to make the best of these opportunities. 
 
Our strategy is focused on building a more robust credit card business, leveraging differentiated 
products, strategic partnerships and digital capabilities as key growth levers. During Q2 of FY27, 
we continue to focus on building a healthy, sustainable and well-balanced portfolio while

maintaining our priorities around profitable customer acquisition, customer engagement,

During this quarter, we augmented our co-branded credit card portfolio with the launch of 
Google Pay Flex SBI Card. This credit card is designed to simplify and elevate the everyday 
payment experience, delivering a convenient blend of rewards, flexibility and security. We also 
launched the Advantage SBI Card on SBI YONO to offer a seamless digital journey that enables 
SBI customers to avail a secured credit card backed by a fixed deposit. 
We continue to roll out customer-centric national and regional offers with many revered brands, 
including Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra, Air India, Bosch, LG, Sony, HP, among others. We 
continued the long-term strategic partnership with Apple for instant discount across different 
Apple products, including the newly launched iPhone 18 Pro. We continue to strengthen our AI 
capabilities across customer engagement, sales and employee productivity. 
 
We are happy to share that CII National Artificial Intelligence (AI) awarded our hyper-
personalization program under the innovative category.  
Coming to the business performance, our robust business model, disciplined portfolio 
management and prudent risk management has enabled us to deliver strong results.  
Let me share the key metrics. Cards in Force have grown to around 2 Crore32 lakhs with 8% 
growth Y-o-Y. 
 
In line with our guidance, we added more than 1 million new accounts during the quarter, 
witnessing 18% increase Y-o-Y. The net card addition for FY27 till August is at 8.6 lakhs new 
cards, which is highest in the industry. We will continue to maintain quarterly run rate of more 
than 1 million new accounts during the year. 
 
Our new account sourcing distribution remains balanced with about 49% sourcing from Banca 
and 51% from open market this quarter. SBI Card continues to be India's second largest credit 
card issuer with Cards in Force market share at 18.5%.  
As regards spends, as per RBI August 2026 data, our spends market share has grown to 19% in 
FY27. Totals spend during the quarter reached INR1,10,689 crores with a growth of around 3% 
year-over-year. 
 
Retail spends reached the highest ever level of INR95,299 crores with a 6% growth Y-o-Y. This 
is despite the festive sales being in Q3 this year and there being a seasonality impact on the Q2 
spend. We have seen robust growth across most POS and online spend categories. Online spends 
contributed 62.8% of the total retail spend in the first half year of financial year, witnessing 
strong growth across discretionary categories. 
 
Key categories include consumer durables, furnishing and hardware, apparel, restaurants and 
jewellery, among others. Corporate spends were at INR15,390 crores during the quarter. UPI 
spends on credit cards continued to grow 17% quarter-over-quarter, majorly in department

Coming to the financial performance for the quarter. Revenue from operations was INR5,141 
crores, registering a 4% Y-o-Y growth. PAT was strong at INR778 crores with an increase of 
75% year-over-year, mainly driven by improved credit costs. 
 
Operating cost during the quarter was INR2,649 crores, with 7% increase Y-o-Y. The cost-to-
income ratio for the quarter was 58.7%, up 193 basis points year-over-year. We expect cost to 
income to remain around 57% to 59% for the year.  
Receivables for the quarter were INR58,376 crores. We continue to focus on building the EMI 
book. With festive season and sales now underway, spends and receivables are expected to pick 
up in Q3 of FY27. The interest-earning assets were stable at 55% with the revolver rate at 22%. 
Portfolio yield for the quarter was 16.1%. The daily weighted average cost of funds for Q2 was 
6.8%. The cost is up by 18 basis points quarter-over-quarter. 
Net interest margin for the quarter was 10.8%. With cost of funds expected to increase over the 
next few quarters, we expect NIM to be range bound. We will continue to optimize our 
borrowing mix to minimize the impact of increase in cost of funds and continue building a bigger 
EMI-based portfolio to keep the NIM stable. 
Speaking about the asset quality, our actions taken over the last 2, 3 years have led to continued 
improvement in the asset mix with NPAs now being the lowest post COVID-19. Continuing the 
reducing trend witnessed over the last 5 quarters, gross credit cost has improved further by 98 
basis points quarter-over-quarter and 342 basis points year-over-year to 5.6%. 
 
Gross NPA has reduced by 14 basis points quarter-over-quarter and 95 basis points year-over-
year to 1.9%. Net NPA is at 0.77%. Slippage ratio is also showing continued reduction. 
Company was carrying an additional provision of INR70 crores up to the previous quarter. 
The prolonged conflict in West Asia and the resulting higher energy prices, inflation and interest 
rates may impact household cash flows. Accordingly, an additional provision of INR30 crores 
has been made to prudently provide for the heightened macroeconomic uncertainty. 
 
With this, the company now carries an additional provision of INR100 crores as of quarter ended 
September 30, 2026. With disciplined customer acquisition, prudent portfolio management, we 
expect gross credit costs to stay around 6% for the current financial year, subject to any adverse 
impact of the ongoing geopolitical crisis on asset quality. Our liquidity position continues to be 
strong. 
Our capital adequacy ratio was at a comfortable level of more than 26%. ROA for the quarter 
was 4.4%, 180 bps higher Y-o-Y, while ROE was at 18.4%, 631 basis points higher Y-o-Y. To 
conclude, India's credit card industry continues to offer significant opportunities for growth, and 
SBI Card is well-positioned to capitalize on this.
